text.p: RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd said on Wednesday it would restructure its management structure into six new global product businesses, with three based in London and three in Australia.
The Anglo-Australian mining house also said the group headquarters would remain in London and the group's Melbourne office would be substantially restructured and its role changed to one of support.
It said about half of the jobs in the Melbourne office would disappear as a result of the restructure. Some of the remaining positions would be transferred to operating locations.
RTZ-CRA said the Melbourne office would support the three product businesses based in Australia -- aluminium (Comalco Ltd) in Brisbane, energy in Melbourne and iron ore in Perth.
The copper, gold and other minerals, and industrial minerals divisions would be based in London.
Kennecott Corp's Salt Lake City, Utah office would be closed and some support services transferred to Kennecott Utah Copper.
The six businesses, together with the worldwide exploration and technology groups, would report to RTZ-CRA chief executive Leon Davis.

Davis said in a statement the new product-based organisation would bring a keener focus on customers and opportunities and would simplify relationships, better concentrate the company's technological expertise and streamline decision making.
"It sharpens our business and makes us more competitive by achieving efficiency gains and cost savings," Davis said.

RTZ-CRA executive chairman Robert Wilson said today's announcement was a major step in furthering the process of integration between RTZ and CRA. He said it would enable the company to realise the full benefits of the merger into a dual-listed company 15 months ago.

"In the enlarged group it has become ever more important to avoid unnecessary layers in the organisation structure and this we are doing in Australia, North America and elsewhere," Wilson said. "It will facilitate a clear focus on business unit performance and our prime objective of creating long-term shareholder value," he said.
The six businesses and their managers are:
- Aluminium, Terry Palmer, Brisbane
- Copper, Jonathon Leslie, London
- Energy, Leigh Clifford, Melbourne
- Gold and other minerals, John Collier, London
- Industrial minierals, Gordon Sage, London
- Iron ore, Mick O'Leary, Perth
RTZ-CRA said the iron business would be headed by Chris Renwick when Mick O'Leary retires in September 1997.
CRA shares were seven cents lower at A$18.38 at 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
